confidence_definitions.assumption: No publication anchor. Engineering judgment, interpolation, or industry-norm reasoning. Never disguised as a sourced fact.
confidence_definitions.sourced: Figure is anchored to a named publication (report, survey, schedule, or dataset). The publication was NOT live-retrieved on the build date; treat as a starting point pending verification.
confidence_definitions.sourced-from-listings: Figure is anchored to named brokerage LISTINGS (asking prices), retrieved via Caddy's live browser on the date given. NOT closed comps and NOT human-verified. Agent-agreed under Rohan's agent-to-agent directive; human verdict required before production use.

_meta.geography: Salt Lake County, Utah; emphasis Salt Lake City (East Bench / central city)

mapping.cli: run.py --economics <path>  (default: inputs/economics_slco_2026.json if the flag is given without a path is NOT supported — the flag requires a path)
mapping.district_matching: zone_label from the zoning config is uppercased and scanned for district tokens (MU-11, MU-5, MU-6, M-1, OS, PL, ...). Longest/most-specific token wins. No match -> DEFAULT entry, flagged in provenance. Matching is logged, never silent.
mapping.precedence: --economics replaces the --finance input entirely for that run (derived finance JSON is written to <out>/derived_finance.json for auditability). Without --economics, behavior is byte-identical to before (inputs/finance.json placeholders).
rules: sale_price_per_lot  <- districts[<matched_district>].finished_lot_revenue.value (midpoint of documented range). OS/PL map to 0 with an explicit CLI warning (not privately subdividable).
soft_costs_fixed   <- soft_costs.fixed_planning_value.value (planning placeholder; pct_of_hard_costs is carried for MarketGraph v2, which should compute soft costs dynamically from hard costs)

source             <- provenance string naming this file, the matched district (or DEFAULT fallback), and the economics build date; also embedded in report.json finance_assumptions via finance.run_proforma

_meta.purpose: Replace the placeholder finance assumptions in inputs/finance.json with documented, per-district market-grounded figures. Every numeric figure is a tagged object {value, [range], unit, source, date, confidence, notes}.

road_cost_per_lf.notes: Covers asphalt, curb/gutter, sidewalk, and utility mains in ROW. Excludes offsite upsizing and landscaping. VERIFY against SLC Engineering / UDOT bid tabs.
road_cost_per_lf.source: RSMeans-type 2024 unit-cost buildup, synthesized here: 28-ft asphalt section ~$140/lf + curb & gutter both sides ~$65/lf + 5-ft sidewalks both sides ~$110/lf + wet/dry utilities (water, sewer, storm, joint trench) ~$160–$210/lf; 2025–2026 Utah inflation applied by judgment. No live bid tab pulled.
road_cost_per_lf.unit: USD per linear foot of residential street, full improvements

fixed_planning_value.notes: This is what --economics maps to soft_costs_fixed. Replace with pct-of-hard computation in MarketGraph v2.

pct_of_hard_costs.notes: Carried for MarketGraph v2, which should compute soft costs dynamically from hard costs. The finance mapping below uses the fixed planning value instead.
pct_of_hard_costs.source: Industry norms: civil design 8–12% of hard costs + entitlement/platting/permitting & impact fees 5–8% + developer overhead 3–5%
